choices.correct_explanation:
• Conduction system of heart consists essentially of certain specialized structures which are responsible for initiation and transmission of cardiac impulses at a higher rate than the rest of the muscle. The following structures are Sino-atrial node (SA node), atrioventricular node, Bundle of His, right and left branches of the bundle block and purkinje fibers.
  • SA node: It is situated in the right atrium at the junction of superior vena cava and the right auricular appendage. It extends downwards along the sulcus terminals for about 2 cm. It generates the normal cardiac impulse at the rate of 70–80 per minute in the adult and acts as a pacemaker of heart and the rhythm originated from this region generally designated as sinus rhythm.        
  • AV node: It is situated in the right atrium at the posterior part of the interatrial septum close to the opening of the coronary sinus. It receives the impulse originating from the SA node and transmits it to the ventricles through the bundle of His. It acts as a reverse pacemaker. The rhythm that is originated in the AV node is known as nodal rhythm. It also initiates the cardiac impulse, but at a slower rate. In abnormal conditions when the SA node fails, the AV node generates the impulse.
  • Bundle of His: The main trunk of this bundle is continuous with the AV node and passes upwards until it reaches the posterior margin of the membranous part of the interventricular septum and then forwards below it. It measures about 20 mm long.

  • Luteinizing hormone is secreted by the adenohypophysis of the pituitary gland.     • Transistor for electronic circuitry was used in second generation computers. One transistor replaced almost 40 vacuum tubes used in the past years.

  • Features of First-Generation Computers (1940–1955)
    • Vacuum tubes and magnetic tapes were used.

    • Punched cards were used to input the data and for getting the output.
    • There was development of machine language and assembly language.
    • Examples: ENIAC, EDVAC and UNIVAC 1
  • Features of Third Generation Computers (1964–1975)
    • Integrated circuits or (ICs) were used in this generation, which were tiny electronic circuits made of semiconductor devices.
    • Keyboards and monitors were invented for input and output.
    • Operating system was designed to run many applications at the same time.
    • Another high-level language PASCAL was developed.
    • Examples: IBM 360 series and 370 series.
  • Features of Fourth Generation Computers (1975–1980)
    • They made use of microprocessors.
    • Several input devices were introduced, like mouse, scanners, microphones, etc.
    • Magnetic disk was used as the primary means of external storage.
    •  Some of the major operating systems, like multiprogramming, online processing was introduced.
    •  The development of graphical user interface (GUI) allowed the users to give commands to the programs just by clicking the icons.
